title: Keller residents, city leadership seek to fight data center in Westlake
text:
At a specially called meeting on Wednesday, residents and city leaders are seeking to stop a project that falls outside Keller's jurisdiction
At a specially called meeting on Wednesday, residents and city leaders are seeking to stop a project that falls outside Keller's jurisdictionAn hours-long meeting stretched into the night on Wednesday, with a packed house full of people wanting to make public comment.
Much of the discussion between leaders was held behind closed doors in an executive session; however, Keller Mayor Ross McMullin addressed the crowd before the executive session, stating that Keller has a right to protect its community.
"I’ll be adding an agenda item for council to consider and authorize formal legal action should Westlake choose to move forward at a future council meeting, because those residents deserve nothing less," said McMullinThe meeting was packed with people hoping to speak, resulting in dozens being moved into an overflow room. "Like many of my neighbors, I’m deeply concerned about the potential health and environmental impacts that this facility could produce, including noise, air and light pollution," said one commenter.
“No one wants to live so close to an AI data center that it will affect their peace, their sleep, their health, and especially the health and development of our children," said another person speaking. The city also circulated a letter sent to Westlake leaders, claiming that by approving the project, they aren't in compliance with city ordinance.
